errors.text: The hypothesis substitutes a refractory Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V-type alloy for the target equimolar Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti powder system.

The proposed 40-60 h milling and SPS below 800 °C substantially conflict with the target process window of 1-6 h milling followed by SPS at 900-1000 °C; sub-800 °C SPS may not adequately densify the proposed refractory alloy.

The falsification experiment does not distinguish grain-boundary strengthening from simple solid-solution strengthening because changing SPS temperature simultaneously changes grain size, density, phase constitution, and possible intermetallic formation.

The predicted ductility above 10% conflicts with the target's high-strength but limited-ductility, intergranular-fracture outcome and is not supported by the cited evidence for a nanocrystalline disordered dual-phase alloy.
